text: Testing plays a vital role in software development. Unit tests check small pieces of code, like individual functions, to ensure they work correctly in isolation. Integration tests then verify that different parts of the system work together smoothly, catching problems that unit tests miss. A popular approach is test-driven development, where you write a failing test first, then code to pass it. Although this takes extra time initially, it saves effort later by reducing bugs. Most importantly, good testing builds confidence. When developers see tests pass, they feel more secure making changes or adding features, knowing that issues will be spotted early, leading to higher-quality software.
